question: What determines how much the heart muscle stretches before it contracts?
explanation: Preload is the stretch of the muscle fibers at the end of diastole, which is directly supplied by the volume of blood returning through the veins. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h1)

question: How does higher afterload affect the heart's workload?

options.A: It slows down electrical signals in the heart
options.B: It decreases the stretch on the muscle fibers
options.C: It raises the resistance the heart must push against to pump blood
options.D: It reduces the oxygen needed by the heart

explanation: Afterload is the pressure threshold that ventricles must overcome to open the valves, meaning higher resistance forces the heart to work harder. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which cells swallow up damaged cholesterol to form fatty streaks in the arteries?
explanation: Macrophages migrate into the blood vessel wall, engulf oxidized low-density lipoproteins, and turn into foam cells that make up the fatty streak. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h2)

question: When a fatty plaque bursts inside a blood vessel, what quickly forms over the area to block it?

options.D: A blood clot and clumped platelets

explanation: Plaque rupture exposes underlying tissue, which immediately activates platelets and the clotting cascade to form an obstructing clot. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h2)

question: What is the main difference in diastolic heart failure compared to systolic failure?

options.A: The upper chambers stretch out first
options.C: The heart cannot fill properly even though its pumping strength is normal
options.D: The heart loses its squeezing power

explanation: Diastolic heart failure happens when stiff ventricles cannot relax enough to fill properly during rest, though the percentage of blood pumped out remains normal. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h3)

question: Why does long-term activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system harm a failing heart?

options.A: It causes the heart muscle to thicken abnormally and hold onto excess fluid
options.B: It destroys red blood cells and causes anemia
options.C: It blocks oxygen from reaching the heart
options.D: It stops the heart's natural pacemaker

explanation: Long-term release of aldosterone and angiotensin II increases blood volume and causes heart muscle walls to thicken and scar, worsening the pump failure. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h3)

question: How do the muscular walls of arteries change during long-term high blood pressure?

options.B: They stretch out and become very thin
options.C: They thicken and narrow the inner channel
options.D: They turn into elastic connective tissue

explanation: Constant high pressure forces arterial walls to adapt by thickening, which reduces the internal diameter of the blood vessel. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h4)

question: Which substance released by damaged blood vessel linings causes them to narrow?
explanation: Damaged blood vessel linings decrease protective widening substances like nitric oxide and increase strong narrowing substances like endothelin, raising blood pressure. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h4)

question: What is an ectopic focus in the heart?

options.A: A physical blockage in a heart artery
options.B: An abnormal pacemaker site outside the main natural pacemaker
options.C: A tear in a heart valve
options.D: An area of dead muscle after a heart attack

explanation: Ectopic foci are irritable cells outside the normal sinoatrial node pathway that spontaneously generate extra electrical impulses. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h5)

question: How do reentry circuits disrupt the normal rhythm of the heart?

options.A: By stopping all electrical activity in the lower chambers
options.B: By turning heart muscle into scar tissue
options.C: By sending signals backward to slow down the natural pacemaker
options.D: By trapping electrical signals in a loop that causes fast heartbeats

explanation: A reentry circuit occurs when an electrical impulse travels in a circle around damaged tissue, endlessly restimulating the heart and causing rapid heart rates. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h5)

question: What happens to a heart valve when it has stenosis?

options.A: The valve does not close all the way, causing leaks
options.B: The outer lining of the heart becomes inflamed
options.C: The valve balloons backward into the upper chamber
options.D: The valve opening narrows and makes it hard for blood to flow forward

explanation: Stenosis refers to stiffened or narrowed valve openings that restrict blood from moving forward smoothly. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h6)

question: A patient has a leaky mitral valve. What happens to their blood when the lower heart chambers squeeze?

options.A: Some blood leaks backward into the upper left chamber
options.B: Blood pools only in the lower right chamber
options.C: Blood flow stops completely across the lungs
options.D: All blood goes straight into the main body artery

explanation: Mitral regurgitation means the mitral valve fails to seal shut during ventricular contraction, allowing blood to flow backward into the left atrium. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h6)

question: Which sign is most common in right-sided heart failure?

options.A: No breath sounds at the top of the left lung
options.B: Sudden wheezing and pink frothy cough
options.C: Swollen neck veins and swollen ankles
options.D: Very high blood pressure with a strong pulse

explanation: Right-sided heart failure backs up blood into the body's veins, leading to swollen legs and distended neck veins. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h7)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with left-sided heart failure. Which finding needs the most urgent attention?

options.B: Crackles in the lower lungs and severe shortness of breath
options.C: Stable blood pressure readings taken hours apart
options.D: Mild swelling in both ankles at the end of the day

explanation: Fluid backing up into the lungs from left-sided failure causes pulmonary congestion, impairing breathing and demanding urgent care. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h7)
